title: Improving communication of diagnostic radiology findings through structured reporting
authors_or_organization: Schwartz LH, Panicek DM, Berk AR, Li Y, Hricak H (Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Center)
data_collection_dates: Conventional reports Jan-Jun 2009; structured reports Jun-Sep 2009
limitations: Single tertiary cancer center; 11 raters (3 radiologists, 3 fellows, 3 surgeons, 2 oncologists); different reports in each arm (not the same cases dictated both ways); outcome is rated satisfaction, not report correctness or downstream decisions; radiologist time to produce reports not measured. Full text read through an automated page-extraction tool; abstract figures cross-checked against Europe PMC abstract.

title: Structured reporting in radiology: a systematic review to explore its potential
authors_or_organization: Nobel JM, van Geel K, Robben SGF (Maastricht UMC+)
limitations: Narrative/thematic synthesis, no meta-analysis (heterogeneity); 63 studies, 61 graded level B; no tally of positive/negative/neutral outcomes; internal inconsistencies in subgroup counts (Results vs Discussion). Final ~9k characters (reference list tail) not read.

title: Cohort study of structured reporting compared with conventional dictation
authors_or_organization: Johnson AJ, Chen MY, Swan JS, Applegate KE, Littenberg B
limitations: Abstract only (Europe PMC). Residents, not attending radiologists; one early-generation point-and-click SRS; cranial MR stroke cases; nonrandomized control vs intervention groups with 4-month repeat reading of the same 25 cases. Accompanying editorial (Langlotz) attributes result partly to early system design (seen only via search summary).

title: The effects of implementing synoptic pathology reporting in cancer diagnosis: a systematic review
authors_or_organization: Sluijter CE, van Lonkhuijzen LRCW, van Slooten HJ, Nagtegaal ID, Overbeek LIH
limitations: All 33 included studies observational (23 cross-sectional, 10 case-control), no RCTs; 8 studies <200 reports; possible publication bias; mostly colorectal and breast; turnaround-time claims rest on references outside the included set; no cost data.

title: Adequacy of surgical pathology reporting of cancer: a College of American Pathologists Q-Probes study of 86 institutions
authors_or_organization: Idowu MO, Bekeris LG, Raab S, Ruby SG, Nakhleh RE (College of American Pathologists)
funding_or_commercial_relationships: Conducted within CAP's fee-based voluntary Q-Probes program (CAP also publishes the protocols)
limitations: Abstract only. Cross-sectional, institution-level association between routine checklist use and complete reports (not causal); voluntary participating institutions; self-reviewed reports.

title: Structured reporting of multiphasic CT for pancreatic cancer: potential effect on staging and surgical planning
authors_or_organization: Brook OR, Brook A, Vollmer CM, Kent TS, Sanchez N, Pedrosa I
limitations: Abstract only. Single institution, retrospective before/after; 3 surgeon raters; surgeons' ratings of sufficiency/ease are judgments, not measured decision accuracy or patient outcomes; time costs not reported.

title: Efficacy of a checklist-style structured radiology reporting template in reducing resident misses on cervical spine computed tomography examinations
authors_or_organization: Lin E, Powell DK, Kagetsu NJ
limitations: Single residency program, retrospective pre/post; changing resident cohorts; possible Hawthorne effect; underpowered for overall effect; fracture misses not reduced. Co-author Powell also authored WS8-S11 (not independent authorship).

title: Prepopulated radiology report templates: a prospective analysis of error rate and turnaround time
authors_or_organization: Hawkins CM, Hall S, Hardin J, Salisbury S, Towbin AJ (Cincinnati Children's Hospital)
limitations: Two-week crossover at one pediatric department; error categories pooled across weeks for many types; manual error logging; dictation time includes interpretation. Same department as WS8-S10 (not fully independent setting).

title: Style and content of CT and MR imaging lumbar spine reports: radiologist and clinician preferences
authors_or_organization: Eskander MG, Leung A, Lee D (London Health Sciences Centre, Ontario)
limitations: Mailed survey with hypothetical reports (stated preference); single center; clinician response 89/183 (49%), radiologist 31/58 (53%); nonrespondents not analyzed; prose samples were themselves highly structured.

title: Improving consistency in radiology reporting through the use of department-wide standardized structured reporting
authors_or_organization: Larson DB, Towbin AJ, Pryor RM, Donnelly LF (Cincinnati Children's Hospital)
limitations: Abstract only. Single-department implementation report; adherence audits measure format conformance, not report correctness or recipient outcomes; radiologist feedback is self-report.

title: State of structured reporting in radiology, a survey
authors_or_organization: Powell DK, Silberzweig JE
limitations: Abstract only. 265/910 (29.1%) response, 90.6% academic; self-reported practices and perceptions (incl. perceived error reduction).

title: Content analysis of reporting templates and free-text radiology reports
authors_or_organization: Hong Y, Kahn CE Jr
limitations: Abstract only. Automated concept annotation (BioPortal) of 5 RSNA templates against reports from one academic center; concept coverage is not clinical importance.

title: Cancer Protocol FAQs (CAP Cancer Protocol Templates)
authors_or_organization: College of American Pathologists
funding_or_commercial_relationships: CAP licenses protocols for use in information systems
limitations: Standard-setter's own FAQ: shows obligations and permitted flexibility, not compliance rates or effects. Page read via automated extraction; live page may change.

title: Adherence to synoptic cancer pathology reporting among pathologists in the National Department of Veterans Affairs Health Care System
authors_or_organization: Ould Ismail AA, Kale S, McGonagle K, Hill B, Pettus JR, DuVall SL, Ferraro JP, Schroeck FR
limitations: Abstract only. Observational audit of 1618 randomly sampled reports in one (large) system; four cancer types; measures format use and element documentation, not downstream effects.

title: Mandatory second opinion surgical pathology at a large referral hospital
authors_or_organization: Kronz JD, Westra WH, Epstein JI (Johns Hopkins)
url: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10590387/ (Cancer 1999;86(11):2426-2435); abstract read via Europe PMC REST API
limitations: Abstract only (PubMed page blocked by cookie wall; Europe PMC abstract used). Changed diagnosis defined narrowly (excludes grade/stage changes), so underestimates all discrepancies; no adjudication against outcomes described in abstract; single referral center; data ~30 years old.

title: Mandatory second opinion in surgical pathology referral material: clinical consequences of major disagreements
authors_or_organization: Manion E, Cohen MB, Weydert J (University of Iowa)
url: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18360282/ (Am J Surg Pathol 2008;32:732-737); abstract read via Europe PMC REST API
limitations: Abstract only. Single institution; disagreement classified by the second-opinion pathologist (who is not a neutral arbiter); clinical follow-up used for significance.

title: Impact of neuroradiologist second opinion on staging and management of head and neck cancer
authors_or_organization: Lysack JT, Hoy M, Hudon ME, Nakoneshny SC, Chandarana SP, Matthews TW, Dort JC
limitations: Retrospective, non-blinded; 94 cases, single center; pathologic gold standard only for 30 surgical cases; second readers had more clinical information and knew the context; time/cost of re-reads not measured.

title: Reducing the rate of repeat imaging: import of outside images to PACS
authors_or_organization: Lu MT, Tellis WM, Fidelman N, Qayyum A, Avrin DE (UCSF)
limitations: Abstract only. Retrospective observational, 267 patients before chemoembolization at one center; small 'not available' group (n=18); adjusted ORs but residual confounding possible (e.g., why images were not imported).

title: 40 CFR Part 312 - Innocent Landowners, Standards for Conducting All Appropriate Inquiries (7-1-20 edition)
authors_or_organization: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (Code of Federal Regulations, via GovInfo)
limitations: Regulation shows required report content and user duties, not compliance, report quality, or whether data-gap disclosure changes buyer behavior. ASTM E1527-21 (the practice most Phase I reports follow) could not be accessed (astm.org returned 403; standard is paywalled).

title: BI-RADS lexicon for US and mammography: interobserver variability and positive predictive value
authors_or_organization: Lazarus E, Mainiero MB, Schepps B, Koelliker SL, Livingston LS
limitations: Abstract only. 5 radiologists, 94 biopsied lesions (enriched sample), single center, BI-RADS 4th edition; authors interpret agreement as 'good' despite fair kappa for final category.

title: Structured Head and Neck CT Angiography Reporting Reduces Resident Revision Rates
authors_or_organization: Johnson TF, Brinjikji W, Doolittle DA, Nagelschneider AA, Welch BT, Kotsenas AL (Mayo Clinic)
data_collection_dates: not reported in abstract (2-month template period)
limitations: Abstract only. Resident-driven QI project; very small structured group (17 reports); revisions are attending corrections of resident preliminary reports (producer-side rework), mostly typographical per authors; trade-press summaries report inconsistent baseline counts (10/41 vs 11/54) - abstract figures used.
